kind: descriptive comparison of two experimental crystal structures (static); no ensemble, population, kinetic, functional-state or treatment-response inference
question: Where along the KRAS backbone does local Calpha geometry differ between GDP-bound (5US4) and GMPPNP-bound (5USJ) KRAS G12D crystal structures with no pharmacological inhibitor modelled, do curvature/torsion, window-matched Calpha distances and proper-rotation local Calpha RMSD locate the same differences, and how much do these locations depend on which crystallographic copies are compared?

GDP.crystallization: sitting drop, 293 K: 100 mg/mL KRAS G12D, 10 mM small-molecule ligand, 4% DMSO; reservoir 0.2 M sodium phosphate dibasic, 20% w/v PEG3350, pH 9.1 (paper Methods; RCSB records the reservoir only). The authors report no electron density for the compound

GNP.crystallization: sitting drop, 293 K: 70 mg/mL KRAS G12D in 0.1 M Bis-Tris pH 5.5, 25% w/v PEG3350 (paper Methods and RCSB)
GNP.incomplete_side_chains: Tyr32 side chain in chains B and F (REMARK 470)

construct: identical entity sequence in both entries: N-terminal His6-thrombin tag (20 residues, numbered -19..0) + KRAS(1-169) with G12D; differs from wild-type KRAS(1-169) (9O0N) only at residue 12 (checked against the 9O0N SEQRES)
ligand_wording: nucleotide (GDP or GMPPNP) and Mg2+ bound in both; no pharmacological inhibitor modelled in either entry. Use 'without a modelled pharmacological inhibitor', not 'ligand-free' or 'apo'. The GDP crystal was grown with 10 mM of a small-molecule compound present (no density reported)
access: PDB archive data CC0 1.0; primary citation Welsch et al., Cell 168:878-889.e29 (2017), doi:10.1016/j.cell.2017.02.006, PMID 28235199, PMC5362268
independent_context: The authors describe both structures as nearly identical to published structures and obtained them while attempting to crystallize an inhibitor complex (Results; Methods 'Protein crystallization'). They give no residue-level comparison between them

mapping.residues: KRAS author numbering 1-59 and 68-166 (158 residues), no insertion codes: the intersection of residues with observed Calpha over all eight chains, fixed from deposition records (REMARK 465) before scoring; the same residue set for every pairing
mapping.gap: 59 -> 68 is a numbering discontinuity by construction; windows spanning it are excluded and reported
mapping.altloc: reject (no alternate locations exist in either entry)

chain_selection.primary: 5US4 chain A vs 5USJ chain A (first deposited chain of each entry; fixed before scoring, not chosen by any score)
chain_selection.sensitivity: all other 11 GDP-chain x GNP-chain pairings, reported in full
chain_selection.copy_context: within-entry copy pairs on the same mapping (5US4 A-B; the 15 pairs of 5USJ chains): magnitude of differences between crystallographic copies with the same nucleotide; descriptive context only
chain_selection.not_replicates: crystal copies are not independent experimental replicates; no test, interval or count across pairings is treated as statistical evidence

windows.three_residue: centered on residue i: (i-1, i, i+1)
windows.four_residue: (i-1, i, i+1, i+2), hinge i -> i+1

metrics.d_kappa: |kappa_GNP - kappa_GDP| (rad), three-residue window, from the TopoFold core
metrics.d_tau: circular |wrap(tau_GNP - tau_GDP)| (rad), four-residue window, from the TopoFold core
metrics.rmsd3: proper-rotation Calpha RMSD of the three-residue window after optimal superposition (MDAnalysis QCP via kras_struct_cmp/rmsd_windows.py) (A)
metrics.rmsd4: the same for the four-residue window (A)
metrics.global_rmsd: Calpha RMSD over all 158 mapped residues after optimal superposition (MDAnalysis QCP), context only

equal_information: every metric uses the same mapped Calpha coordinates (adapter output) for the same residues; a window is reported for all metrics of its size only where kappa (three-residue) or tau (four-residue) is valid in both structures
reporting: residue-mapped table for the primary pair, with min/median/max of each metric over the 12 GDP x GNP pairings and the max over the 16 within-entry copy pairs
per metric: the ten largest primary windows; for each window, in how many of the 12 pairings it is among that pairing's ten largest (descriptive recurrence, not a test)
Spearman rank correlation between metrics on shared windows: primary value and range over the 12 pairings (descriptive)
exclusions (windows spanning the 59->68 gap or chain ends) with cause
figure: per-window profiles (primary line, range over pairings, copy-pair maximum) and a superposed Calpha trace of the primary pair coloured by three-residue RMSD

cross-study comparison with KRAS-STRUCT-1 read from its frozen table (not recomputed): Spearman between the two studies' per-window profiles on windows present in both, and overlap of the ten largest windows per metric (descriptive)
permitted_interpretation: Direct geometric differences between these crystal structures. Confounded by crystal form and packing (H 3 with two copies vs P 1 with six copies), crystallization pH (9.1 vs 5.5) and additives, resolution (1.83 vs 1.94 A), disordered Switch-II residues 60-67 (unobserved in at least one chain and therefore excluded), and coordinate error. Copy-to-copy differences show the size of non-nucleotide variation within one crystal, not replicate variability of an experiment. No ensemble, population, kinetic, functional-state or treatment-response claim; nucleotide identity does not establish functional state. Differences between KRAS-STRUCT-1 and KRAS-STRUCT-2 are not attributable to inhibitor binding or to the G12D mutation, which are not independently controlled across the studies. Agreement with familiar switch-region locations is not independent biological validation.
